limitations: Shared machine with other agent workloads; load average differed between rounds (round 2 about 6-7 at the start of pass 1, then about 1.5-2.6; round 1 about 4-10). Differences of a few percent between rounds, including the ts run-to-run drift (up to about 6.5 percent on p95), are within this noise. Not portable to other hardware.

The 300 s idle hold covers only the large-100 profile viewer prototype on darwin-arm64, measured with /usr/bin/time -l (10 ms CPU resolution) after subtracting a 2 s control hold. It does not represent the product TUI with a live agent connection, probing or file watching, so it does not settle the spec 15.1 idle CPU budget. Three reps per candidate.

Latencies include Python spawn and pyte pty overhead (control floors of about 2.3 ms spawn and 4.0-4.3 ms pty path); pyte answers only DA/DSR queries so a real terminal could change ts first-frame time. Keystroke latency includes pty and scheduler delay.
RSS is macOS max RSS from /usr/bin/time -l, not comparable to Linux RSS or Windows working set. Idle memory over time was not measured separately.
Cold start after reboot or purged page cache was not measured; cold_first_exec rows only compare the first run of a freshly copied file with later ones.

ts clean-environment results (darwin, linux-arm64, linux-x64, musl probe) are reused from round 1, not re-run; justified because the ts artifact sha256 values are identical for all four targets. The fake-agent contact counts in the round-2 clean runs cover go and rust only (4 connections each); the note string inside clean-darwin.json still says 6 because it is a fixed string in clean_env.py.
linux-x64 ran emulated (amd64 under an arm64 Docker Desktop VM), proving loading and behavior only, not native x86-64 speed or behavior.

Native Windows execution is blocked: no Windows host. Windows artifacts were inspected for file type, size, sha256 and PE headers only; nothing about Windows named-pipe, console or signal behavior is established.
macOS artifacts are ad-hoc signed only; Gatekeeper/quarantine behavior for downloaded files was not tested, and writes outside the fresh TMPDIR/HOME/cwd were not traced.
Conformance counts (go and rust 133p/0f/0e on darwin and linux; ts 126p/7f/0e darwin and 127p/6f/0e linux) are quoted from the task packet and were not re-verified here.

Round-1 to round-2 changes for go and rust are reported as measured; the cause of the go TUI-workload RSS drop (-8.2 percent) and the rust keystroke p95 increase (+13.7 percent, 0.3 ms) was not investigated and may be noise.
jsonschema is not installed in the venv, so the record was checked for required keys but not validated against record.schema.json with a validator.
